chunks: From him, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjāl, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqbah, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to one of his freed slaves: 'O 'Abdullah, preserve your honor.' He said: 'And what is my honor, may I be your ransom?' He said: 'Your morning journey to your market and your honoring of yourself.' And he said to another of his freed slaves: 'Why do I see you have left your morning journey to your honor?' He said: 'I intended to attend a funeral.' He said: 'Then do not neglect the journey to your honor.'
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq consider to be the source of a person's honor and dignity in daily life?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines 'izz' (dignity) not as passive status but as the active pursuit of honest livelihood through daily trade. He illustrates that even essential social duties like attending funerals should not become an excuse to abandon one's professional responsibilities, thereby linking economic self-sufficiency directly to spiritual and social honor in Shia ethical tradition.
